## What it is

The Incident Response policy states what the organization requires for incident response and who is accountable for it. It meets [IR-1](/controls/ir/ir-1/) through the sections every family policy shares, and adds one statement group per control. Each baseline variant includes only the controls in that baseline, taken from the NIST SP 800-53B profiles.

Adopt the ready-to-adopt edition: fill every highlighted field, delete any "Federal systems" section that does not apply, and have the accountable official approve it. The annotated edition adds guidance on why each section exists and what assessors look for.

## Decisions to make first

The policy has 31 organization-defined parameters across all variants; each appears as a highlighted field with its typical value where one is given. Settle these first:

| Decision | Controls | Typical | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who runs incident response, and who is on call outside business hours? | [IR-4](/controls/ir/ir-4/), [IR-7](/controls/ir/ir-7/) | An internal incident response team with a named lead and an on-call rotation, backed by a retained incident response provider for major incidents. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Which outside parties must be notified of an incident, and who decides to notify them? | [IR-6](/controls/ir/ir-6/) | Regulators, customers and partners named in laws and contracts; legal counsel decides, with the Chief Information Security Officer. | Chief Information Security Officer |

Record your values in the [Incident Response decision worksheet](/templates/worksheets/ir/), which lists every parameter with its typical value.

## Preview (Moderate baseline, annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
The sections before and after Policy statements meet IR-1, which asks for a policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination and compliance, plus procedures, dissemination, a designated official and a review cycle. Assessors check each element, so keep every section even when it is short. Each statement cites the IR-1 item it meets. If you adopt several family policies, the same sections repeat in each; that is expected, and it lets each policy stand alone.
:::

### Purpose

This policy states what <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> requires for Incident Response, and who is accountable for meeting those requirements. (IR-1a.1(a))

### Scope

This policy applies at the <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level</span> to every system that <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> owns or operates, or that is operated on its behalf, and to every person with access to those systems, including employees, contractors and partners. (IR-1a.1(a))

### Roles and responsibilities

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is accountable for this policy and shall approve exceptions to it. (IR-1a.1(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the incident response policy and procedures</span> shall manage the development, documentation and dissemination of this policy and its procedures. (IR-1b)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement this policy for their system and document how in the system security plan. (IR-1a.1(a))
- Each person within scope shall follow this policy and report suspected violations to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>. (IR-1a.1(a))

### Management commitment

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> approves this policy and shall provide the resources needed to implement it. (IR-1a.1(a))

### Coordination

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate this policy with the legal, privacy, human resources and procurement functions, and with the owners of related policies, before each approval. (IR-1a.1(a))

### Compliance

- This policy shall be consistent with the laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards and guidelines that apply to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>, including <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: laws, regulations and standards that apply to the organization</span>. (IR-1a.1(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review compliance with this policy through the organization's assessment and continuous monitoring activities. (IR-1a.1(a))
- An exception to this policy shall be requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with its compensating measures. (IR-1a.1(a))
- Violations of this policy shall be handled through the organization's sanctions process. (IR-1a.1(a))

### Procedures

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the incident response policy and procedures</span> shall ensure that documented procedures exist to implement this policy and its associated controls. (IR-1a.2)

### Dissemination

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the incident response policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the incident response policy is to be disseminated</span>. (IR-1a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the incident response policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate the procedures that implement this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the incident response procedures are to be disseminated</span>. (IR-1a)

### Policy statements

:::note[Guidance]
Each statement below comes from the clause for one control or enhancement in the chosen baseline. The reference at the end of each statement names the control item it meets.
:::

#### Incident response training (IR-2)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall provide incident response training, consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities, to system users within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: a time period within which incident response training is to be provided to system users assuming an incident response role or responsibility <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 30 days</span></span> of their assuming an incident response role or responsibility or acquiring system access. (IR-2a.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall provide that training when system changes require it. (IR-2a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall provide that training <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency at which to provide incident response training to users <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span> thereafter. (IR-2a.3)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall review and update incident response training content <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency at which to review and update incident response training content <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that initiate a review of the incident response training content <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a change to the incident response plan, and lessons learned from an incident or exercise</span></span>. (IR-2b)

#### Incident response testing (IR-3)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall test the effectiveness of the incident response capability for the system <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency at which to test the effectiveness of the incident response capability for the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span> using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: tests used to test the effectiveness of the incident response capability for the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a tabletop exercise based on a realistic scenario, and a functional test of notification and escalation</span></span>. (IR-3)

#### Coordination with related plans (IR-3(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall coordinate incident response testing with the organizational elements responsible for related plans, such as contingency, continuity and crisis communications plans. (IR-3(2))

#### Incident handling (IR-4)

:::note[Guidance]
The phases in IR-4a follow the incident handling life cycle NIST describes for incident response; the Incident Response Plan template carries the detail. Assessors ask for records of recent incidents that show each phase, and for evidence that a lesson learned changed a procedure.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall implement an incident handling capability, consistent with the incident response plan, that includes preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication and recovery. (IR-4a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall coordinate incident handling activities with contingency planning activities. (IR-4b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall incorporate lessons learned from incident handling into incident response procedures, training and testing, and implement the resulting changes. (IR-4c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall ensure the rigor, intensity, scope and results of incident handling are comparable and predictable across the organization. (IR-4d)

#### Automated incident handling processes (IR-4(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall support the incident handling process using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms used to support the incident handling process <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the case management system and automated playbooks in the security operations platform</span></span>. (IR-4(1))

#### Incident monitoring (IR-5)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall track and document incidents. (IR-5)

#### Incident reporting (IR-6)

- All personnel shall report suspected incidents to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period for personnel to report suspected incidents to the organizational incident response capability <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 1 hour of discovery</span></span>. (IR-6a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall report incident information to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: authorities to whom incident information is to be reported <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: senior leadership, legal counsel, and any regulator, customer or partner that law or contract requires be notified</span></span>. (IR-6b)

<div class="tpl-federal">

##### Federal systems

Federal agencies notify the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) of incidents under FISMA (44 U.S.C. §§ 3553 and 3554). As of September 2026, the [CISA Federal Incident Notification Guidelines](https://www.cisa.gov/federal-incident-notification-guidelines) (effective April 1, 2017) set the time frame: within one hour of the incident being identified by the agency's top-level incident response team, security operations center or IT department.

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall report incidents to CISA within one hour of identification, as the CISA Federal Incident Notification Guidelines require. (IR-6b)

</div>

#### Automated reporting (IR-6(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall report incidents using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms used for reporting incidents <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the incident reporting form and case management system, which notify the incident response team automatically</span></span>. (IR-6(1))

#### Supply chain coordination (IR-6(3))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall provide incident information to the provider of the product or service, and to other organizations in the supply chain, for system components related to an incident. (IR-6(3))

#### Incident response assistance (IR-7)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall provide an incident response support resource, as part of the incident response capability, that offers system users advice and assistance with handling and reporting incidents. (IR-7)

#### Automation support for availability of information and support (IR-7(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Incident response team</span> shall increase the availability of incident response information and support using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms used to increase the availability of incident response information and support <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a self-service reporting portal and an incident response page on the intranet</span></span>. (IR-7(1))

#### Incident response plan (IR-8)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall develop an incident response plan that provides a roadmap for implementing the incident response capability. (IR-8a.1)
- The plan shall describe the structure and organization of the incident response capability. (IR-8a.2)
- The plan shall describe at a high level how the incident response capability fits into the overall organization. (IR-8a.3)
- The plan shall meet the organization's unique requirements related to its mission, size, structure and functions. (IR-8a.4)
- The plan shall define reportable incidents. (IR-8a.5)
- The plan shall provide metrics for measuring the incident response capability. (IR-8a.6)
- The plan shall define the resources and management support needed to maintain and mature the incident response capability. (IR-8a.7)
- The plan shall address the sharing of incident information. (IR-8a.8)
- The plan shall be reviewed and approved by <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles that review and approve the incident response plan <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the Chief Information Security Officer</span></span> <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review and approve the incident response plan <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually</span></span>. (IR-8a.9)
- The plan shall explicitly designate responsibility for incident response to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: entities, personnel, or roles with designated responsibility for incident response <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the incident response team, led by its designated lead</span></span>. (IR-8a.10)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall distribute copies of the plan to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: incident response personnel (identified by name and/or by role) to whom copies of the incident response plan are to be distributed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the incident response team members, by role</span></span> and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: organizational elements to which copies of the incident response plan are to be distributed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the security operations, legal, communications and human resources functions</span></span>. (IR-8b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall update the plan to address system and organizational changes, and problems found during its implementation, execution or testing. (IR-8c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall communicate changes to the plan to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: incident response personnel (identified by name and/or by role) and organizational elements <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: everyone who received the plan</span></span>. (IR-8d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall protect the plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification. (IR-8e)

### Review and update

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the incident response policy and procedures</span> shall review and update this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current incident response policy is reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require the current incident response policy to be reviewed and updated</span>. (IR-1c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the incident response policy and procedures</span> shall review and update the procedures that implement this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current incident response procedures are reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require the incident response procedures to be reviewed and updated</span>. (IR-1c.2)

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

For federal information systems, this policy also carries out the agency's information security responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 ([44 U.S.C. § 3554](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim), Federal agency responsibilities) and [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf), Appendix I, Responsibilities for Protecting and Managing Federal Information Resources.

- Where the agency's organization-wide policy sets a value for a parameter in this policy, each system shall use that value or a stricter one. (IR-1a.1(b))

</div>
